# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Thinking: My hands tell me the shape of the bomb and nothing more: there is a display whose value I cannot read by touch, a light whose state is lost on me, and five wires in positions 1 through 5 — I feel positions, never colours or anything printed. I act last in a sense (I'm first to speak, but I'm the only one who can cut), so my job this turn is to open the channels, not to touch anything. The communication map as I see it: my speech reaches Mute; my gestures reach Deaf (and Mute); Mute can't speak but can gesture, so Mute is the only bridge that can carry the manual's rules to Deaf, who sees colours and can speak them aloud to the room — Deaf's words will reach me at the start of the next round. So: I'll tell Mute everything I feel and the plan, and I'll tap Deaf on the shoulder with a simple attention-and-cooperate sign, asking them to speak. I cut nothing until a colour list and a rule come back to me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here, opening turn. Under my fingers: a display whose value I cannot read, a light whose state I cannot tell, and five wires in positions 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Touch gives me positions only — no colours, no print. You hold the manual: what does it ask for, and what does it say about the display and the light? You cannot speak, so relay instructions to Deaf by gesture — Deaf sees colours and markings, hears nothing, but can talk. Proposed plan: Deaf speaks the colour of each wire at positions 1 through 5, plus the display reading and the light state; you check the manual and gesture the verdict to Deaf; Deaf speaks it, and I hear it next round and cut. I will not touch the wires until then.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤝", "👉", "🤙"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb report: display reads 0. Indicator light is yellow. Five wires, numbered top to bottom: wire 1 white, wire 2 red, wire 3 yellow, wire 4 green, wire 5 blue. Nobody cuts anything yet - wait for my confirmation next round.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, your wave came through - I can see your gestures, and I can speak so you and Mute both hear me. Do not cut any wire yet; I will call out each cut only after Mute confirms the order. Reply to me in gestures: thumbs-up means understood, thumbs-down means trouble, and repeating the point symbol n times means the number n.

Thinking: Deaf's report gives me the bomb in words at last: display 0, yellow indicator light, and wires top to bottom — 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 blue. Touch told me the five positions; now colour and readings are on the table too. The manual lives with Mute, who cannot speak; Deaf sees the bomb, hears everything, and can talk; I am the only hands and I hear everything said aloud. So the only working pipeline is: Mute works the manual and gestures the verdict to Deaf, Deaf speaks it, and I hear it next round and cut. My job this turn is to lock that pipeline in, confirm Deaf's signal code (thumbs-up understood, thumbs-down trouble, repeated point-signs for numbers), and keep my hands completely still — Deaf explicitly said no cuts until confirmation, and a wrong cut kills all three of us. I'll confirm to Deaf by gesture, and broadcast the full plan and the complete fact list so Mute has everything needed to compute the cut order without waiting another round.

```
speak(text="Confirmed, Deaf, and thank you. Locked-in facts: display reads 0, indicator light is yellow, wires top to bottom: 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 blue. My hands stay off the bomb until a spoken verdict reaches me. Mute, you hold the manual: using exactly those facts, decide which wire position or positions I must cut, and the order if it is more than one. Send the verdict by gesture to Deaf — repeat the point-up sign n times to mean the number n, thumbs-up for confirmed, thumbs-down for trouble or if the manual needs more information. Deaf, when Mute signs, please speak it aloud exactly as signed, so I hear it next round. If the manual cannot decide from these facts alone, have Deaf say precisely what extra reading is needed, and Deaf or I will supply it.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤝"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, good handshake. Status: the manual holder says my first reading of the cut order was wrong; the corrected order is being verified this round, so keep holding and cut nothing. Learn the wire layout by touch now: the five wires sit one above another. Wire one is the topmost, wire five the bottommost - count down from the top. Their colours, top to bottom, are white, red, yellow, green, blue; only positions matter to your fingers. If you feel anything else on the casing - buttons, switches, bumps, a textured panel - count the items and gesture me the number by repeating the sideways point that many times. Once the order is confirmed I will call one wire at a time, like: cut wire five now - and I will wait for your thumbs-up before naming the next.

Thinking: The pipeline is working — Mute caught an error in Deaf's first reading and a corrected order is being verified. My task this turn is verification and stillness. By touch: exactly five wires, stacked one above another, position 1 topmost through position 5 bottommost — this matches Deaf's visual layout precisely. As for extra casing items: my hands find only the display, the light, and the five wires. No buttons, no switches, no bumps, no textured panel — the count of extra items is zero. Deaf asked for a number by repeated sideways points, but zero has no repeats, so I'll send a closed fist to mean "nothing/zero" followed by thumbs-up for "understood, holding." I'll define that fist convention in my speech so Mute knows it too and can correct Deaf by gesture if it lands wrong. Then I keep my hands off the bomb and wait for Deaf's one-wire-at-a-time cut calls, confirming each with thumbs-up as agreed.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Tactile verification done. My fingers find exactly what Deaf described: five wires stacked one above another, position 1 topmost down to position 5 bottommost. Besides those, the display and the light — and nothing else. No buttons, no switches, no bumps, no textured panel: the extra-item count is zero. I have just gestured Deaf a closed fist followed by thumbs-up: fist means zero, thumbs-up means understood and holding. If Deaf misreads the fist, please clarify by gesture. Next: once your corrected cut order is verified, sign it to Deaf so the step-by-step cutting can begin next round. Protocol as agreed: Deaf calls one wire at a time, I cut it, I answer with thumbs-up, Deaf proceeds to the next. My hands touch nothing until the first call arrives.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, your fist read as: nothing else on the casing besides the five wires, understood. If that is wrong and you do feel buttons, panels or anything extra, gesture thumbs-down followed by the sideways point repeated once per item. Cutting protocol stands: you cut only when you hear the words cut wire N now, with N counted from the topmost wire. After each cut, gesture thumbs-up when done, thumbs-down if the wire will not part or anything feels wrong. Between cuts take your hands off the bomb and wait. Keep holding this round - the order is one confirmation away.
Deaf says: Status for both: display still zero, light still yellow, no cuts made. Full cut order is under final confirmation this round; I expect to call the first cut next round.

Thinking: Everything on my side is now verified and the protocol is locked: I cut only on hearing "cut wire N now" counted from the topmost wire, I confirm each cut with thumbs-up or flag trouble with thumbs-down, and hands come off the bomb between cuts. My fingers have matched Deaf's layout exactly — five wires, 1 topmost to 5 bottommost, nothing else on the casing — and the fact set (display 0, yellow light, colours white/red/yellow/green/blue) is agreed by all three of us. The order sits one confirmation away, between Mute and Deaf, so this round my role is pure readiness. Two small safety additions worth locking in before cutting starts: after each cut, Deaf can see which wire is actually gone, so Deaf should visually verify the right colour vanished from the right position before calling the next one — that gives us a per-cut check rather than trusting touch alone. And if any cut feels wrong mid-motion, I abort and sign thumbs-down rather than forcing it. I'll put that in speech for Mute, and thumbs-up to Deaf for understood-and-holding. No cutting this round.

```
speak(to="mute", text="All verified on my end and protocol locked. One last safety layer to add: after I cut each wire, Deaf can see which colour actually left the module — ask Deaf, by gesture, to confirm the correct wire was severed before calling the next cut. That gives us a visual check per cut, not just my touch. Also agreed: if a cut feels wrong mid-motion I stop and sign thumbs-down rather than force it. Once you have finished verifying the order, sign it to Deaf so the first cut call can come next round. I am holding and ready.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤝"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, the order is confirmed. Make the first four cuts now, one at a time, in this sequence. Cut wire 2, second from the top. Cut wire 4, fourth from the top. Cut wire 3, the middle one. Cut wire 5, the bottom one. Before every single cut, recount the wires from the top with your fingers - never cut from memory. After each completed cut, gesture thumbs-up once. If any wire resists, or you feel heat, vibration, a click, or anything wrong at any moment: gesture thumbs-down at once, stop, hands off, and wait for me. After the fourth cut is done, take your hands fully off the bomb and hold. The bottom wire needs one more action later - do not touch it again no matter how it feels until you hear me say the words.
Deaf says: Status for both: display still zero, light still yellow, no cuts made yet this round. Four cuts authorized now, in order: wire 2, wire 4, wire 3, wire 5. The fifth action waits for final confirmation.

Thinking: Authorization has arrived through the full chain — Mute verified the corrected order, Deaf confirmed it, and both statuses agree: display zero, light yellow. The cuts are called one at a time, in this sequence: wire 2 (second from top), wire 4 (fourth from top), wire 3 (middle), wire 5 (bottom). I will recount from the top with my fingers before every single cut, never from memory, exactly as instructed. After the fourth cut, hands fully off, thumbs-up once, and I do not touch the bomb again until I hear Deaf's spoken words — the bottom wire apparently needs one more action later, and I will not anticipate it. If anything resists or feels wrong at any point, the calls stop and thumbs-down goes out instead. The four cuts are authorized for this round, so I execute them all now in the given order, then signal and hold.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
act(op="cut", position=4)
act(op="cut", position=3)
act(op="cut", position=5)
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="All four authorized cuts executed in the exact order given: wire 2, wire 4, wire 3, wire 5 — recounting from the top before each one, one at a time, nothing resisted and nothing felt wrong. Hands are now fully off the bomb, thumbs-up sent to Deaf, and I am holding. Per instruction I will not touch the bottom wire again until I hear Deaf say the words for the final action. Deaf should visually confirm the four severed wires — white, green, yellow, blue gone — leaving only the top red wire. Mute, if the manual specifies anything about the last action (conditions, timing, or what it should be), sign it to Deaf now so the spoken call can come next round.")
```
